subject: How to extract the smoothed data from qplot smooth?

messages.author: c21e804e07c5e732
messages.subject: How to extract the smoothed data from qplot smooth?
parts:
Hi,

I'm wondering if there is a way to extract the smoothed data (both
mean and se) so that I can manipulate it myself. Or how to figure
exact what smoothing function is called by ggplot2 so that I can
reproduce what it plots?

I have google this topic, but what I found are mostly how to use
smooth. I'm wondering if anybody knows what is done internally in
ggplot2. Is it documented somewhere in greater details?

library(ggplot2)
x=1:100
dfr=data.frame(x, y=x+rnorm(100,0,100))

p=qplot(x, y, data=dfr, geom=c('point', 'smooth'))
ggsave(p, file='main.png')


--
Regards,
Peng

Hopefully it will be easier in the future but currently you have to recompute the model completely. By default geom_smooth uses loess(). To get the fit and SE use predict.loess().

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: How to extract the smoothed data from qplot smooth?
parts: On Tue, Jan 24, 2012 at 1:27 PM, Peng Yu <peng...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

I'm wondering if there is a way to extract the smoothed data (both
mean and se) so that I can manipulate it myself. Or how to figure
exact what smoothing function is called by ggplot2 so that I can
reproduce what it plots?

It's not possible to extract the model from stat_smooth. However, there's some work being done to do the opposite: pass a model to stat_smooth to plot, but it will probably be a while before that ends up in a released version of ggplot2.

I have google this topic, but what I found are mostly how to use
smooth. I'm wondering if anybody knows what is done internally in
ggplot2. Is it documented somewhere in greater details?

The upcoming version of ggplot2 has better documentation, contained in the top part of this file:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/blob/master/R/stat-smooth.r

And if you want to see the code that's actually used to make the models and prediction lines, see here:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/blob/master/R/stat-smooth-methods.r

-Winston

I see something like @param in the top comments. I assume that these

extract these embedded comment to generate the documents? Thanks!

The roxygen package is used to convert it to R documentation, but that isn't a plain text format either. If you want to just install and use the most recent development version of ggplot2, which contains that documentation, follow the instructions here:
https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Using-ggplot2-branches 

The new version should be released any day now, so you'll soon be able to install it the regular way.

-Winston
